scope_note: Light verification pass. Broad Asparagaceae is morphologically heterogeneous under APG/Kew circumscription. The project's live local pool is Yucca-only, while Joey provides useful Agave/Yucca/Hesperaloe family-context material. Teach Yucca as a local Agavoideae-style anchor, not as the definition of all Asparagaceae.

joey_coverage.audit_summary: Strong Agave/Yucca/Hesperaloe morphology, rosettes, teeth, terminal spines, inflorescences and flowers.
joey_coverage.assessment: Joey coverage sufficient; classification/overfit protection is the main task.

family_lesson.broad_family_rule: Asparagaceae in the modern APG/Kew sense is heterogeneous. Flowers often have 6 tepals and 6 stamens, a 3-locular ovary that may be superior or inferior, and capsule or berry fruit, but vegetative form varies dramatically.
family_lesson.local_yucca_rule: For the local Yucca lesson, start with a basal/terminal rosette of stiff fibrous leaves, margin fibers and/or terminal spine, then inspect the large terminal panicle, 3+3 fleshy tepals, 6 stamens and 3-carpellate fruit.
avoid_overgeneralizing: Do not teach rosette + spine as universal Asparagaceae.
Do not assume ovary position is fixed across broad Asparagaceae.
Do not use Agave/Yucca/Hesperaloe as separate families; the broad modern family includes former Agavaceae.
Do not treat the audit's Agave/Hesperaloe context as live local source-pool genera when the current pool is Yucca-only.

taxonomy_cleanup.issue: Live pool contains both Yucca treculeana and Yucca treculiana spellings.
taxonomy_cleanup.current_kew: Yucca treculiana Carrière is accepted by current Kew/POWO.
taxonomy_cleanup.action: Flag Yucca treculeana for source-row orthographic/taxonomic reconciliation; do not create a duplicate learner species.

confusable_families.Amaryllidaceae: Often bulbous with pseudoumbellate inflorescences enclosed by spathaceous bracts; compare reproductive architecture rather than leaf shape alone.
confusable_families.Liliaceae: Both may show 3+3 tepals and 6 stamens; local Yucca is distinguished by woody/rosette architecture and genus-level flower/fruit characters.
confusable_families.Cactaceae: Yucca has true fibrous leaves in a rosette and lacks cactus areoles.
